nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-critical (1000000000)
nodes.rationale: Storage layer (Ceph OSD/mon/mgr) underpins every PVC; eviction means data unavailability, so it sits highest of the five in-cluster tiers but still below system-cluster-critical.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-platform (900000000)
nodes.rationale: Stateful core that everything else depends on: Postgres, MariaDB/MaxScale, Envoy ingress, step-ca.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-high (100000)
nodes.rationale: Observability and shared services (monitoring, Harbor, Redis, poolers) — important but recoverable if evicted.

nodes.label: PriorityClass feather-low (-10)
nodes.rationale: Negative value so best-effort apps (bluemap, node-red, uptime-kuma) are preempted/evicted before anything else under pressure.

nodes.label: Cluster workload priority tier scheme (5 levels)
nodes.rationale: All five tiers deliberately sit below the built-in system-cluster-critical (2000000000) / system-node-critical (2000001000), which stay reserved for kube-system; higher value wins on preemption and eviction ordering.

nodes.label: ReferenceGrant allow-s3-proxy (rook-ceph-fr01)
nodes.rationale: Cross-namespace backendRef from storage-proxy HTTPRoutes to the RGW Service in rook-ceph-fr01 is only legal with this grant; both HTTPRoutes reuse the single grant.

nodes.label: HTTPRoute rgw-internal (s3.apps.onelite.feather)
nodes.rationale: s3.apps.onelite.feather is deliberately NOT in the CephObjectStore dnsNames, so RGW serves it path-style; resolves via the *.apps.onelite.feather wildcard to the 10.200.90.1 gateway LB and requires clients to trust the step-ca root CA.

nodes.label: SecurityPolicy rgw-external-proxy-cors
nodes.rationale: Envoy Gateway CORS policy limited to https://outline.onelitefeather.dev so Outline's browser uploads/downloads against the RGW endpoint work with credentials and Range requests.

nodes.label: Envoy Gateway eg (envoy namespace, https listener)
cert-manager enableGatewayAPI ControllerConfiguration
nodes.rationale: cert-manager >=1.15 enables Gateway API via file-based config, not the old ExperimentalGatewayAPISupport feature gate (a no-op since 1.15) which left HTTP-01 gatewayHTTPRoute challenges failing with 'gateway api is not enabled'. Gateway API CRDs must exist before the controller starts (provided by envoy-crds); Helm rolls the controller on this config change so the startup check picks them up.

nodes.label: Controller HA via leader election (replicaCount 2)
nodes.rationale: Active/standby: leader election is mandatory with replicaCount > 1, otherwise the replicas fight over tunnel config and DNS records.

nodes.label: cloudflared connector pods (controller-generated Deployment)
nodes.rationale: The connector Deployment is generated by the controller (not Helm) with a minimal pod spec and reconciled every ~10s, so node-spreading cannot be enforced via config — only the controller pods get explicit pod anti-affinity.

nodes.label: cloudflared --proxy-keepalive-timeout=10m
nodes.rationale: Default 90s keepalive on the connector->origin connection made bursty origins (BlueMap S3 tile uploads) pay a full TCP+TLS reconnect (~700ms observed) after idle gaps. Applies to ALL hosts behind this shared connector.

nodes.label: cloudflaredServiceMonitor (metrics on :44483)
nodes.rationale: cloudflared already runs its Prometheus endpoint (the controller sets --metrics itself, not Helm-configurable); this only wires scraping. No tracing equivalent exists: cloudflared's OTel spans go only to Cloudflare's edge, per cloudflare/cloudflared#671.

nodes.label: Deployment barman-cloud resource patch (cnpg-system)
nodes.rationale: The upstream barman-cloud plugin manifest ships no resources, leaving it BestEffort; requests/limits are injected so it is not first to be evicted.

nodes.label: Staged PrometheusAgent teardown (two-step migration to Alloy)
nodes.rationale: Step 1 removes only the PrometheusAgent CR while the operator still runs, so its finalizer reconcile tears down the agent StatefulSet/PVCs. The generated StatefulSet has no ownerReference to the CR, so disabling the operator in the same apply would leave old agent pods double-writing to Mimir alongside alloy-metrics forever. Step 2 (prometheusOperator.enabled: false) only after the StatefulSet is confirmed gone.

nodes.label: kubeApiServer duration-histogram bucket drop rule
nodes.rationale: Apiserver duration-histogram buckets alone were ~127k of ~275k active series and pushed Mimir into its per-tenant series limit; _sum/_count survive so rates and averages still work.

nodes.label: kube-state-metrics (Flux-aware config, 384Mi limit)
nodes.rationale: Confirmed live: 128Mi OOMKilled the pod within 1s of startup once customResourceState was added — watching/caching all Flux CRDs cluster-wide needs headroom on top of the standard collector set.

nodes.label: gotk_resource_info customResourceState metrics for Flux CRs
nodes.rationale: gotk_resource_info is not a native Flux controller metric but a kube-state-metrics feature the Flux Cluster Stats dashboard was built for. Deliberately does not set collectors/--custom-resource-state-only, which would replace the chart's full collector list and break every other kube-state-metrics-backed dashboard.

nodes.label: cnpg_backup_* gauges from Backup CRs
nodes.rationale: Plugin-based (barman-cloud) backups never update the operator's cnpg_collector_last_available/failed_backup_timestamp metrics — confirmed live they stay 0 forever. Backup CRs are the only reliable source; nilIsZero is required because stoppedAt stays unset on in-progress/failed backups.

nodes.label: MetalLB upstream native manifests kustomization (v0.15.3)
nodes.rationale: Upstream MetalLB manifests ship no requests/limits, leaving controller and speakers BestEffort — first to be evicted, which would drop BGP announcements; modest requests + memory limits are injected via patches.

nodes.label: HelmRelease step-certificates (SOPS-encrypted values: step-ca root/intermediate, provisioners)
nodes.rationale: The whole HelmRelease patch is SOPS-encrypted because its values embed the step-ca root/intermediate CA material and provisioner keys.

hyperedges.label: RGW S3 exposure through the Envoy gateway (external + internal routes, cross-namespace grant, CORS)
MetalLB BGP LoadBalancer path: pool -> advertisement -> per-zone peers announced by speakers
Flux/CNPG observability without Prometheus Agent: KSM customResourceState scraped by Alloy into Mimir
